checkpoints.question: Why can `note.txt` still be read after the first volume-writing container exits?
checkpoints.model_answer: A named volume outlives a container. Another container can mount the same volume and read files stored there.

evidence.label: Persist one file in a named volume

checkpoints.question: How does a bind mount differ from a named volume?
checkpoints.model_answer: A bind mount exposes a chosen base-station path. Docker manages a named volume separately from a chosen host filesystem path.

checkpoints.question: Why does this LX use a read-only bind mount?
checkpoints.model_answer: It lets a container inspect host files without permission to modify them, limiting accidental or unnecessary host changes.
